newsitem.title: USA: GKN's Meineke sees appeal taking 18 months.
newsitem.headline: GKN's Meineke sees appeal taking 18 months.

text.p: An appeal by GKN Plc's Meineke Discount Muffler Shops against a $600 million judgment against it would likely take at least 18 months, Meineke's top lawyer said Friday.
"This is begging to be appealed," Meineke chief counsel Ted Pearce said in a telephone interview. "The appeal would last 18 months or more."

Pearce said several secondary issues still before the trial judge must be resolved before an appeal of the judgment, the largest commercial damages award ever against a British company, can be taken to a higher U.S. court.
He gave no forecast of when an appeal would be filed.
Meineke was assessed the damages and interest Thursday by a federal judge in Charlotte, N.C., headquarters of Meineke.
The judge, acting under a North Carolina law, tripled compensatory damages of $197 million awarded in December by a jury that found Meineke had committed breach of contract, negligence and fraud.

The damages were won by Meineke's 2,500 franchisees in the United States, who alleged that the auto-muffler retailer had mishandled and misappropriated millions of dollars charged the franchisees for advertising.
GKN said earlier today in London that it would appeal the decision and would make a provision of 270 million pounds ($434.2 million) as exceptional charges in its 1996 accounts.
"This includes interest and legal costs likely to accrue pending the outcome of the appeal and will be treated as an exceptional charge in the 1996 accounts," GKN said in a written statement.
